narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

ENTRY: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claims to have last entered the United States illegally by walking across the International Boundary Line between the United States and Mexico in February of 2004 near Nogales, AZ. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] has no proof that this is when he actually entered the United States, and there is no record stating that this was in fact his last entry date. TRAVEL: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] states that he found a smuggler in Nogales, Sonora, Mexico and made the arrangements to be smuggled into the United States for $1500.00. One evening he and a group of two other subjects walked across the International Boundary Line outside of Nogales, AZ. They walked for three hours to a small town and entered a house. They spent two days in this house and were picked up at the house by an unknown subject in a car. They were then driven to Albuquerque, NM. They did not pass through, or drive around, any U.S. Border Patrol checkpoints on this journey. He spent one day in a trailer in Albuquerque. He then boarded a bus and traveled to Chicago, IL. From Chicago, he boarded another bus to Detroit, MI. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] has lived and worked in the Detroit area ever since. He currently resides in Auburn Hills, MI. INADMISSIBILITY: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] is a citizen of Mexico. He has never had any documents that would allow him to be, or remain, in the United States legally. FACTS OF ARREST: On May 2, 2017 Border Patrol Agent (BPA) [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] were [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] At approximately 7:50 AM a dark colored van passed the agents. The agents noted that the van appeared to be heavily laden and the windows were tinted. As the van passed, the driver looked away from the agents, as if he did not want the agents to see his face. The agents decided to take a closer look at the van. As the agents caught up to the van, they pulled up alongside the passenger side window and paralleled the van for approximately one half of a mile. The agents noted that there were two males in the front of the van. The front seat passenger was sitting rigid in his seat, staring straight ahead through the windshield. As the agents continued to parallel the van, the passenger started turning his head away from the agents, as if he did not want to make eye contact with them. [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] The agents also noted that there was no conversation going on between the occupants of this van. [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] The agents fell in behind the van and ran a registration check through Detroit Sector Dispatch on the MI license plate displayed on the rear of the van [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . The agents were advised that the van was not reported stolen and was registered to a female out of Clarkston. As far as the agents could see, there was not a female present. Many times illegal aliens have vehicles registered to a third party as they are not able to, or have fear of, registering a vehicle in their names because of their immigration status.

As the agents were behind the van, they could see through the right-side rear window, as it was tinted lighter than the other windows. They could not see any silhouettes of persons riding in the rear of the van. The agents pulled up alongside the passenger side of the van once again. They observed the same behaviors as they did earlier. The passenger was looking away from them and there was no conversation going on amongst the two visible occupants. All of the sudden the driver exited at the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] exit. The agents were able to quickly maneuver and follow. As they were following the van up the exit ramp, they saw the silhouette of a head come up in the rear of the van. The agents began to suspect that there may in fact be more subjects laying down in the rear of the van, attempting to hide from the agents view. This [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] The agents suspected that some type of criminal activity was afoot based on what they had witnessed thus far. The agents decided to initiate a vehicle stop to further investigate. BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] activated the emergency lights and sirens and the van yielded at the intersection of [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] The agents approached and BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] identified them as United States Border Patrol Agents. After a brief field interview, BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] determined that three of the four subjects in the van were citizens of Mexico, not in possession of any valid immigration documents that would allow them to be, or remain, in the United States legally. These subjects were taken into custody at that time. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was one of these subjects. The van was turned over to a fourth subject who was found to be legally present in the United States. All four subjects were transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station for processing. EMPLOYMENT: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] works for [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] out of Pontiac, MI. He earns $12.00 per hour. At the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] fingerprints and biographical data were entered into the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] computer systems. These systems revealed the following:

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

06/28/1995: [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] shows subject was arrested; location unknown 03/14/1998: USBP Chula Vista, CA04/28/1999; processed as a VR 04/28/1999: USBP Douglas, AZ; processed as a VR CRIMINAL HISTORY: None found. HEALTH: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claims to be, and appears to be, in good health. DISPOSITION: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was processed as a WA/NTA without bond. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was advised of his rights per form I-826. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] signed form I-826 indicating that he wants to see an immigration judge. He was offered a stipulated removal and he declined. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was given a list of Pro Bono Legal Service Providers. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was advised of his right to speak to the Mexican Consulate. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he did not want to speak to the Mexican Consulate. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was transferred to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail along with his property and money. Jail space was approved by Deputy [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)]
